In September 1657 AD Shah Jahan fell, triggering a struggle for succession between his
four sons; Dara Shikoh, Murad Bakhsh, Shah Shuja, and Aurangzeb Alamgir. The victor,
AurangzebAlamgir,declared himselfemperorin1658ADandstrictlyconfinedShahJahan
in Agra Fort until his death.
Aurangzeb Alamgir:The Last of the Great Mughals
AurangzebAlamgiris considered thelastgreat Mughal ruler.His rulelastedforalmostfifty
years 1658 AD -1707 AD. When he became Emperor, he inherited a magnificent empire,
splendid cities, forts and palaces. Aurangzeb was an eminent scholar. He knew Arabic,
Persian,Turkishand Sanskrit.Like otherMughal Princes,he was trained in calligraphyand
art. Under his rule, the Mughal empire expanded to the parts of Afghanistan and Burma.
Do You Know?
Aurangzeb's original name was Muhi-al-Din Muhammad.His kingly title was
Alamgir meaning"Jewel in the Throne".He was born in 1618 AD,at Dhod, Malwa
in India.Hewas crownedasanEmperor in1658ADand hediedin1707AD.
Historians divide Aurangzeb's reign into two parts. In the first part of his reign i.e. until
1680AD,hewas devoted to safeguarding the empire fromrebellions and disintegration.
After 1680 AD, Aurangzeb seemed to have changed his policies and attitude and became
very strict. As you read this unit you will discover some of the ways in which Aurangzeb
changedthetraditions ofMughalrulers beforehim.
